title: Do we still need cinemas?
situation: An international film magazine has invited readers to send in opinion pieces on the following statement: "In the age of streaming, nobody needs cinemas any more." The best contributions will be published in next month's issue. Write your opinion piece for the magazine.
situationHu: Egy nemzetközi filmmagazin olvasói véleményeket kér arról az állításról, hogy a streaming korában már senkinek sincs szüksége mozikra.

points.text: describe how you and your friends usually watch films
explain why streaming services have become so popular
argue what cinemas can offer that watching at home cannot
say whether you agree with the statement and predict the future of cinemas

usefulPhrases.hu: egy ültő helyében végignézni egy sorozatot

usefulPhrases.en: at the click of a button
Cinemas will survive as long as …

checklistExtra: Világosan kiderül, egyetértek-e az állítással, és ezt a befejezésben is megerősítettem?

modelAnswer.text:
Why the Big Screen Still Matters

Like most teenagers I know, I watch nearly all my films on my laptop or phone, and I often binge-watch a whole series in one weekend. My friends and I only go to the cinema together a few times a year, mainly to see big blockbusters.

It is hardly surprising that streaming services have become so popular. For the price of a single cinema ticket, you get a whole month of films and series, available at the click of a button. You can watch whenever you like, pause for a snack and choose from thousands of titles without leaving your sofa.

Nevertheless, cinemas offer something that no living room can. First of all, there is the big-screen experience: the huge picture and powerful sound make an action film far more impressive. Secondly, in a dark room without notifications, you actually concentrate on the story. Most importantly, going to the cinema is a shared experience – laughing or screaming together with a hundred strangers is something you simply cannot recreate at home.

For these reasons, I do not agree that nobody needs cinemas any more. I am convinced that they will survive, although they will probably have to change, offering more special events such as premieres, film festivals and live concerts. As long as cinemas give people a reason to leave home, they will always have an audience.
